summary: Thinh Canh Quang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of the West in 2007. He studied under Lewis Lancaster, Ananda W. P. Guruge, and doctoral supervisor Kottegoda S. Warnasuriya.

Thinley Dorji Bhutia worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and Chief Editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology in 1994, and earlier was Tibetan Teacher and Boarding Superintendent at Darjeeling Government High School.

Thomas A. Forsthoefel is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Georgetown University, Loyola University Chicago, and the University of Chicago (PhD 1998, under Paul J. Griffiths), later becoming an associate professor of religious studies at Mercyhurst University around 1999.

Thomas A. Tweed is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at Stanford University (1984) under William R. Hutchison and others. He served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (circa 1993–2008).

Thomas Borchert works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He was a PhD candidate at the University of Chicago from around 1999 to 2006, and around 2006 he became Associate Professor of Religion at the University of Vermont.

Thomas Burrow (1909–1986) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. Educated at Queen Elizabeth School and Christ's College, Cambridge, he served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Oxford from around 1944 to 1976.
Thomas Cleary (1949–2021) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Harvard University until around 1975, where he was taught by E. Bruce Brooks.
Thomas E. Crow is an art historian who studied at Pomona College from 1965 to 1969. He held academic posts at the University of Michigan (circa 1990–1996) and New York University (circa 2007).

Sir Thomas Edward Colebrooke (1813–1890) was an Indologist and historian educated at Eton College and the East India Company College. He served as President of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland from 1864 to 1890.

Thomas Freeman Yarnall is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Educated at the University of Washington and Columbia University (PhD 2003, under Robert A. F. Thurman), he later served as Executive Editor in Columbia's Department of Religion.

Thomas H. Doctor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and conducted doctoral research at the University of Lausanne under Tom J. F. Tillemans. He has held a post at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Thomas James Mazanec specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Calvin University, earned an MA at the University of Colorado Boulder (2011), and completed his PhD at Princeton University (2017) supervised by Anna M. Shields and Stephen F. Teiser.

Thomas Jülch is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich around 2006 to 2011 and worked as a research fellow at Ghent University from around 2012 to 2017.

Thomas Nathan Patton is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Cornell University (circa 2007–2013) under Anne M. Blackburn and held a post at the City University of Hong Kong from around 2016 to 2021.
Thomas Oberlies is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Albrecht Wezler. He holds a post at the University of Freiburg.
Thomas P. Kasulis specializes in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He has held academic posts at Ashland University and Ohio State University, where he became a professor around 1991.

Thomas R. H. Havens is a historian and Japanologist. He held positions at Connecticut College (circa 1966–1991), the University of Illinois System (circa 1991–1999), University of California, Berkeley (circa 1999), and Northeastern University (circa 2004).

Thomas Sheehan specializes in philosophy and religious studies, with education from Fordham University and UC Berkeley. He served as Professor of Philosophy at Loyola University Chicago (1972–1999) and Professor of Religious Studies at Stanford University (1999–2017).

Thomas Watters (1840–1901) was a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his education in Ireland, studying at Queen's University Belfast in 1857 and earning a B.A. from Queen's University of Ireland around 1857–1862.

Thomas William Rhys Davids (1843–1922) earned a PhD at the University of Breslau. He founded the Pali Text Society and SOAS, and held professorial posts at University College London and the University of Manchester.
